messages:
sam: quick heads-up — judge selection is causing CI flakiness on the 0.9-quant bringup. failing in eval-runner job eval/llm-judge/compare_metrics, looks like tie-break path triggers nondeterministically.

jake: ugh, saw a red recently. can you paste the runner logs?

sam: gist of failure:
```
INFO runner: starting compare_metrics run
INFO judge-selector: chosen judges=[oracle-small, referee-v2]
WARN tie-break: ambiguous scores 0.72 vs 0.72
ERROR adjudicator: inconsistent_decision, fallback applied
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"runner/eval.py\", line 312, in run
    result = judge_pool.adjudicate(batch)
  File \"judge/pool.py\", line 87, in adjudicate
    raise InconsistentDecisionError
InconsistentDecisionError: intransitive votes
```

sam: job url: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/1234 (eval/llm-judge/compare_metrics)

oliver: that trace suggests nondeterministic tie-breaker ordering. I think the new tie-break heuristic using model confidence+length has an unstable comparator for NaNs.

jake: we saw something similar when quantized judges produced identical logits due to aggressive rounding. can you repro locally with `--seed`?

sam: repro steps I ran:
1) checkout feature/quant-bringup
2) docker-compose run eval-runner
3) ./runner --suite judge --model referee-v2-quant --seed 0 --batch-size 16
-> sometimes passes, sometimes hits the InconsistentDecisionError

eva: ci-bot posted this last night too. attaching the CI artifacts (judge logits csv).

ci-bot: Job eval/llm-judge/compare_metrics failed: see artifacts at https://ci.internal/artifacts/1234/judge_logits.csv :warning:

oliver: can you share a tiny repro script? if it's seed-sensitive we should make the runner enforce deterministic hashing and stable sort in tie-breaker.

sam: quick repro attached inline:
```python
# tiny_repro.py
import random, numpy as np
random.seed(0)
np.random.seed(0)
# simulate quantized logits collision
logits = [round(x,2) for x in np.linspace(0.72,0.72,10)]
# tie-breaker: sort by (score, confidence) but confidence is nan for some judges
entries = [(i, logits[i], float('nan') if i%3==0 else 0.5) for i in range(len(logits))]
entries.sort(key=lambda x: (x[1], x[2]))
print(entries)
```

jake: yep the `nan` sorting explains it. in python `nan` compares oddly. two fixes: coerce nans to -inf or use stable sort and explicit fallback order.

oliver: for CI we should:
- patch judge-selector to sanitize confidence: `confidence = -1 if math.isnan(confidence) else confidence`
- add a stable deterministic tie-break fallback: prefer judge with smaller stable id
- add a unit test that runs 1000 randomized seeds and fails on nondeterminism

sam: agreed. also think we should add logging telemetry: when fallback tie-breaker fires, emit metric `judge.tie_breaker.fallback` with tags model=referee-v2-quant, quant=8bit. that will let Optimize/Console teams see regressions in real workloads.

eva: can we gate the CI so that flakiness doesn't block merges? maybe mark the test as flaky and have a flaky-assertion that triggers an infra ticket instead of blocking.

jake: +1 for flaky marker. but we should also fail fast on InconsistentDecisionError for now so we catch regressions. change CI job to `allow_failure: true` for branch deploys and `allow_failure: false` for release branches.

sam: I'll open a PR with the sanitizer + deterministic fallback + extra unit test. assigning to @oliver for review. PR will include:
- code fix in judge/pool.py (sanitize nans)
- stable id tie-breaker in judge/resolve.py
- new test in tests/test_tiebreak_determinism.py (seed sweep)
- CI tweak: mark job as flaky in .gitlab-ci.yml for feature branches

oliver: sounds good. also let's add an evaluation dashboard panel: fraction of adjudications that hit fallback per day. Eva / product can use that to detect quality regressions after quantized bringups.

eva: will add a panel to the judge-metrics dashboard and alert if rate > 0.5% for 24h.

sam: thanks all — PR shortly. I'll include sample artifacts and notes on how to reproduce locally. :thumbsup:

jake: ping me when PR is ready, I'll run the branch through a seeded stress job.

ci-bot: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/repo/pulls/456 (sam -> main)

sam: closing the loop, PR merged, patch deployed to staging, running 10k seeded runs now. will follow up if anything else crops up.

oliver: nice work. we should also add a lint rule to catch `math.isnan` usage without sanitization in judge code.

sam: added to backlog.
